Every gate in this system is a model choosing to comply. Nothing can refuse.

in execution order. GROUNDING is what must be read before anything is produced — inputs arrive on their own, grounding is what gets skipped.

ACCEPTANCE — two keys
PRODUCT
Frame the intent
sherpa Explore
UNUSED
an idea, a product, a feature, an enhancement, a thought,
a question, a comparison to another product or repo — or
an issue or a complaint.
TRIAGED into one of three routes:
NEW — idea / feature / enhancement
PROBLEM — issue / complaint / something broken
OUT — a question about the product. answered from
product truth, NOT framed as new work.
captured by interview, uploaded evidence, or a whiteboard
session. the two routes converge on the same output shape.
PROBLEM route MUST read the CURRENT situation first —
code, infra, product specs — and then do the gap analysis.
no proposal before the present state is read.
NEW route: the competitor scan, and the evidence of need.
there may be no current situation to read.
sensei is a TOOL, not a MUST. invoked when its route
matches: asserting a position, proving a gap or an idea
with measurement, or a complex problem needing point of
cause and 5 whys — triggered by a problem that survived
a few attempts to fix it. otherwise avoided.
same rule for superpowers and every other external tool:
it declares the route it serves, and is invoked on match.
TWO documents, not one shape with optional sections.
both are a .md — machine-read, long-read, measurable,
handoff-ready — AND a diagram. the SECTIONS differ,
not the artifact types.
IDEA BRIEF: what it is · what it must become · what gap
it addresses · how it compares to other products · its
value · a viability SIGNAL, not a verdict · next inputs.
PROBLEM STATEMENT: what is happening now, READ from code,
infra and specs, not assumed · what should be happening ·
the gap between them, MEASURED · point of cause, if the
sensei trigger fired · the value of closing it · next inputs.
TWO KEYS, neither sufficient alone. the routes converge
here: shared machinery, route-specific checklist.
MACHINE: the sections are present — WHICH sections depends
on the route · the measurements are stated · the diagram
conforms to the pattern it claims · the next stage's
declared inputs are all filled.
HUMAN: Tony says approve.
any gap or risk that could not be closed is documented
AND confirmed. carried is fine — silent is not.
HANDOFF: both routes go to Test viability. the killer
assumption differs, the test does not — a problem going
straight to design is the jump-to-countermeasure failure.
Test viability
interrogate /
sherpa Validate
UNUSED
the framed artifact — idea brief or problem statement —
its killer assumption, and the viability SIGNAL from
framing. never a verdict; testing it is this rung's job.
what counts as KILLER differs by route:
IDEA — is the need real, and can we win?
PROBLEM — is the cause correctly located, and is
closing the gap worth what it costs?
risks are NOT unnamed — that was a drafted claim and it was
wrong. they are unmitigated, unqualified, or accepted
unknowns. UNQUALIFIED is the dangerous one: a named,
unsized risk reads as managed because it is written down.
EVIDENCE is what qualifies a risk — a TEST or an ANALYSIS,
whichever is cheaper and would actually change the decision.
analysis is evidence: not everything needs an experiment.
two passes, or 'risk-driven' becomes a full risk register:
1. cheap estimate, to triage what could be fatal
2. real evidence for those candidates only
QUALIFIED = proven AND measured. three fields, never one:
proven by — the test or the analysis
impact — measured, in the units VALUE was stated in
likelihood — separately. do NOT multiply it by impact:
expected value is the wrong maths for a bet
taken once. 5% of ending it is not 5% damage.
FATAL = impact >= the value framing declared, at any
likelihood. likelihood sets the RESPONSE, not the class.
A RISK WITHOUT A COUNTERMEASURE IS A BLOCKER. that is the
default, so silence STOPS the work rather than passing it.
each risk therefore lands in one of three:
COUNTERMEASURE, PERMANENT — root cause addressed
COUNTERMEASURE, TEMPORARY — contained, not cured. carries
the condition that brings it back. an unmarked temporary
countermeasure is a permanent one by neglect.
BLOCKER — no countermeasure. clears ONLY by an explicit
act of acceptance: who, when, and on what basis. an
accepted UNKNOWN is a blocker accepted without even
knowing its size — allowed, but never by default.
THE LIMIT ON ACCEPTANCE: high impact + high likelihood +
no countermeasure = DEAD PROJECT. not a kill you choose,
a state you recognise. every other blocker may be accepted
by name; this one may not, or acceptance becomes an escape
hatch for anything. only RESHAPE or KILL remain.
verdict: proceed only when NO unaccepted blocker remains.
otherwise reshape, or kill. a kill here is a SUCCESS —
the cheapest place the thing can die.
MACHINE: nothing is merely NAMED. every risk is proven,
measured and given a likelihood, or is an explicit accepted
unknown. impact and value are in comparable units. every
countermeasure states what it is expected to do — it is a
hypothesis, so it must be checkable later. every TEMPORARY
countermeasure carries its return condition. no blocker is
unaccepted.
HUMAN: Tony accepts each blocker BY NAME — including the
unknowns and any low-likelihood fatal. rounding a low
probability to zero silently is what this gate stops.
an UNQUALIFIED risk reaching the next stage is the exact
failure this function exists to prevent.
Hold product truth
CUT
shipped changes from build,
release slices

CUT. it failed its own test: asked whether any
question had ever needed answering that the CODE
could not answer, the answer was no. a document
restating mechanism is a second source that drifts,
and a drifted doc answers confidently and wrongly.
— not yet interviewed —
Slice a release ·
Set the goal
sherpa Launch
UNUSED
what is already built · the framed and viability-tested
candidates · their QUALIFIED risks with countermeasures
attached, from Test viability · and the record of what
was already ruled out.
risk arrives PRE-CHEWED. do not re-assess it here: a
feature carrying a TEMPORARY countermeasure is a different
slicing candidate from one carrying a permanent fix.
the five things that actually decide a grouping, and they
do not all work the same way:
HARD CONSTRAINT — dependency. forbids groupings outright.
B cannot ship before A if B needs A. no trade-off.
CEILING — how much change a user can absorb AT ONCE.
a release can be too big even when everything in it is
finished. almost nothing enforces this, which is why
'we shipped everything we had' is a real failure mode.
the bound comes from the RECEIVING side, not capacity.
TRADE-OFFS — effort, risk, opportunity. these shape the
grouping among what is left, they do not forbid it.
THE GROUPING. a release is a GROUPING, not a time axis —
time may be attached later, or never. MVP / v1 / v1.2 are
ordered, not scheduled. conflating the two turns a
grouping decision into a deadline argument.
THE DONE CONDITION — assembled, never authored. every
item is a conformance check against an upstream
declaration:
met the feature spec <- the contract
met the product spec <- the idea brief
goal of the function met <- the goal set here
looks EXACTLY like design <- design, approved pre-build
tests pass <- every proof layer declared
by Decide what proves it, INCLUDING user testing
documentation complete <- DERIVED, not declared:
every declaration covered — feature, product and
problem specs, the changes and fixes implemented,
the solution diagrams, and what we ruled out
MACHINE: every item in DONE points at a declaration that
EXISTS. nothing in DONE that nothing declared — an
unbacked item cannot be checked, so it passes by
assertion, which is the unqualified-risk failure again.
dependencies are satisfied by the ordering. the slice is
within the comprehension ceiling.
HUMAN: Tony approves the grouping — what is in, what is
deferred, and why this cut rather than another.
Choose what matters next
— nothing —
GAP
the open work — everything not yet done, from every
release grouping. plus, for each item, the VALUE that
framing declared for it.
the failure is NOT bad ranking. it is that the items are
not in a form you can weigh. three things missing, and
only one of them is about order:
NO DIAGRAM — rendered, not prose
NO CLEAR STRUCTURE — same shape per item, so they are
actually comparable
NO CLEAR ASK — what decision is wanted, per item
'too much noise' is not volume. a list of prose titles
gives you nothing to weigh, however short it is.
items BLOCKED on a dependency are not candidates at all —
a dependency is a hard constraint, so they cannot be
'next' at any consequence. draw them apart.
candidates on TWO CONSTANT AXES, both about OUTCOME:
CONSEQUENCE — what it costs us NOT to do it
VALUE — what we gain by doing it. already declared
by Frame the intent and already used by
Test viability. third caller, not a new
measure.
and, per item, WHAT WE LOSE by not choosing it. v0.68's
rule applied to work: name the loss, or it disappears into
the good news. a ranked list shows what you picked and
never what you gave up.
EFFORT IS NOT AN AXIS. it is an INPUT measure beside two
OUTCOME measures, which makes the grid incoherent, and it
systematically flatters cheap work. it survives as a
tiebreaker inside a cell, and as one of the five slicing
factors at Slice a release.
MACHINE: every candidate carries consequence, value and
its loss. blocked items are separated, not ranked. the
view is RENDERED — prose fails this by construction.
HUMAN: Tony can weigh them at a glance and say which.
the test is not 'is the ranking right'. it is 'can he
compare them at all'. an item he cannot understand
without opening it fails, however well it is ranked.
DESIGN
Design the solution
superpowers
brainstorming
EXTERNAL
stage 1's declarations, arriving together:
the INTENT DOCUMENT — idea brief or problem statement —
with its MEASUREMENTS. those numbers are what the package
must answer, and what post-build conformance will measure
against.
the QUALIFIED RISKS with countermeasures attached, from
Test viability. a countermeasure is a CONSTRAINT on the
shape — design builds around it, not a note in a document
nobody opens.
read BEFORE proposing any approach:
WHAT WE RULED OUT — so a dead option is not re-pitched.
THE ACTUAL CODE — not summaries. the 08-02 failure: a
stale code comment trusted twice while the design doc
holding the answer went unread.
STANDING DECISIONS — conventions already agreed that a
design cannot violate. without them, settled ground gets
re-litigated.
LIVING DESIGN DOCS of whatever the work touches — the
exact class whose retrieval failed on 08-02. the code
cannot tell you WHY a neighbouring piece has its shape.
second caller for reachability.
ONE PACKAGE from ONE conversation — not four functions.
(the draft split — shape / agree / prove / interface —
was Claude's decomposition of the brainstorming checklist,
never Tony's shape.)
detailed specs · architecture plans · testing strategy ·
solution diagrams · flow diagrams · visualizations for
as many aspects as we can.
at least TWO approaches with trade-offs before one is
chosen — on constant axes, costs marked, bets named,
resolved in ONE message.
LIVES AT docs/design/<slug>.md + .excalidraw — living,
undated, same slug as the product doc, so the pair is
derivable. (chosen over folder-per-piece-of-work, 08-03.)
TWO KEYS, neither sufficient alone:
HUMAN: every aspect Tony cares about is DRAWN, he has
reviewed the drawings, and nothing is left to annotate.
MACHINE: every measurement stage 1 declared has a NAMED
ANSWER in the package — point at where the design delivers
it. the MEASURING itself is post-build conformance, not
here. nothing declared upstream goes unaddressed.
GO writes a dated gate record — docs/gates/<date>-<slug>-
design.md — and hands to CONTRACT (stage 3), where the
score is written. NEVER to writing-plans: the working
half of brainstorming exits into the dead half today.
CONTRACT
Write the contract ·
Size and assign
conductor
OK
the GO'd design package, arriving INTACT — full specs,
documents, diagrams, measurements, plans, UX design,
systems. nothing summarized on the way in: the contract
is written FROM upstream truth, not from a digest of it.
the qualified risks ride with it — a countermeasure is a
constraint the work order must build around.
the TERRAIN the work will change — the actual code, read
not summarized. the order must name exact paths,
signatures and values, and it cannot do that from memory.
WHAT WE RULED OUT — a contract proposes implementation
choices, so it reads the record like everything else
that proposes.
STANDING DECISIONS — the conventions a work order
cannot violate.
THE WRITTEN WORK ORDER: implementable by a builder who
NEVER SAW THE REASONING. every piece carries its exact
scope, the why behind any non-obvious choice, and ITS
OWN CHECK. sized and assigned AFTER the piece is written
— a tag assigned during planning measures how hard the
piece felt, not what judgment survived being written down.
TWO-TIER ACCESS, by role:
the OVERSEER holds all upstream truth.
a BUILDER gets the exact spec for their piece plus
access to related materials — AND NO MORE.
MACHINE, and machine ALONE when it holds: every piece is
measurable against an upstream declaration — the design
package, the measurements, the countermeasures. NO HUMAN
GATE at this rung, provided that measuring is real.
(Tony, 2026-08-03: 'i dont need to approve contract if
we can measure it meets output of other stages.')
a piece NOTHING upstream declared cannot be measured, so
it cannot pass by assertion — it is a PUSH-BACK to
design. the DONE-assembled rule applied to the contract.
ESCALATION CONTRACT: the human hears ONLY of a gap no
agent role can answer that is a BLOCKER — the blocker-
acceptance path from Test viability. otherwise the next
report is GOAL ACHIEVED.

9. Requirements — first cut
one MUST per function. shallow on purpose: enough to expose how they depend on each other, not enough to be a spec. (?) = drafted, not read
PRODUCT
Frame the intent
MUST state why this exists in terms checkable by someone outside the build,
and be reachable by the design rung without asking a question
Test viability
MUST qualify every candidate-fatal risk with EVIDENCE — a test or an
analysis — and record impact and likelihood SEPARATELY, never multiplied.
FATAL = impact >= the value framing declared, at any likelihood.
MUST leave every risk in one state: countermeasure (permanent or
TEMPORARY, carrying its return condition), accepted, accepted unknown
(by whom, when, why not gathered), or fatal.
MUST NOT let an UNQUALIFIED risk reach the next stage — a named, unsized
risk reads as managed, which is the failure mode this exists to stop.
Hold product truth — CUT 2026-08-03
CUT. the code is the truth for mechanism and sequencing; a parallel
document is a second source that drifts. the one measured failure behind
this function was RETRIEVAL, not absence — the document existed.
what survives goes elsewhere: retrieval is the 'reachable' clause of
Where the work is written down; intent and value are already produced
by Frame the intent.
RETURN CONDITION: a question arises that the code cannot answer.
Slice a release · Set the goal
a release is a GROUPING, not a time axis — time may be attached later, or
never. ordering and scheduling are separable.
MUST respect dependencies as HARD constraints, and MUST cap the slice at
what a user can absorb at once — a release can be too big even when
everything in it is finished.
MUST consume the qualified risks from Test viability rather than
re-assessing them.
The DONE condition MUST be ASSEMBLED from upstream declarations, never
authored at the end: every item is a conformance check against something
already declared. MUST NOT contain an item nothing declared — it cannot
be checked, so it passes by assertion.
Choose what matters next
MUST present candidates on two constant axes, both about OUTCOME:
CONSEQUENCE (what it costs us not to do it) and VALUE (what we gain).
MUST NOT use EFFORT as an axis — an input measure beside outcome measures
makes the grid incoherent and flatters cheap work.
MUST name, per item, WHAT WE LOSE by not choosing it — a ranked list shows
what you picked and never what you gave up.
MUST be RENDERED, with the same structure per item and a clear ask. the
failure is not bad ranking, it is items that cannot be weighed: no diagram,
no structure, no ask.
MUST separate items BLOCKED on a dependency — they are not candidates at
any consequence.
MUST NOT rank by what fits the session about to run.
DESIGN
Design the solution
MUST produce ONE package: detailed specs, architecture plans, testing
strategy — and diagrams for as many aspects as we can. agreed in
diagrams, not prose.
MUST propose at least two approaches with trade-offs before one is
chosen — options on constant axes, costs marked, bets named, resolved
in ONE message, not a sequence of clarifications.
MUST be approved before any build starts, on TWO KEYS: every aspect
drawn and nothing left to annotate · every stage-1 measurement has a
NAMED ANSWER in the package. the measuring itself is post-build.
MUST live at docs/design/<slug> — living, undated, same slug as the
product doc. GO writes a dated gate record and hands to CONTRACT,
never to a plan-writing skill.
MUST state test bias per layer, and name every seam needing a
contract test.
(?) MUST output interface values a machine can check — tokens, hex,
spacing, states
CONTRACT
Write the contract · Size and assign
MUST be implementable by a builder that never saw the reasoning;
every piece carries its own check.
MUST tier access: the overseer holds ALL upstream truth; a builder
gets the exact spec for their piece plus related materials, NO MORE.
MUST size and assign AFTER the piece is written, never before.
MUST NOT need human approval — provided every piece is measurable
against an upstream declaration. an unmeasurable piece cannot ride
through on assertion: it is a push-back to design.
MUST escalate to the human only a BLOCKER no agent role can answer;
otherwise the next report is goal achieved.
BUILD
Execute a unit · Prove it worked
MUST produce evidence, and MUST check collateral — what changed that
should not have, not just whether the intended change landed
Review unanchored
MUST see only the spec and the diff. No session context, ever.
Refuse bad work
MUST be able to block, from outside the model.
Advisory output does not satisfy this.
Verify against what we said
MUST check every declared layer — code, logic, architecture, pixel, product
measurements — and report conformance per layer, not one verdict
SESSION
Open / close · Keep tempo · Hold state
MUST survive going cold — the next session picks up without re-deriving
Route to the altitude
MUST decide before the work is sized, not after
Drive to done (/goal + /loop)
MUST stop at the stated hand-back point.
MUST NOT run at all where nothing can refuse.
Keep context optimal (inside the loop)
MUST cut on token headroom AND on quality degrading or drifting from
intent. (?) the second has no signal — self-correction rate is the
nearest proxy we have, and it was added for another reason
CROSS-CUTTING
How we talk to each other
MUST be one question, drilled, carrying the findings it depends on.
(?) MUST be agreed in diagrams, not prose — constant axes, colour marking
cost only, bets named and discharged by name, containment over arrows,
an altitude shift between movements.
(?) MUST round-trip: the diagram goes out, annotations come back as
input, preserved across regeneration.
(?) MUST pick a story format before drawing — proposal / compare-contrast
(current → new → what changes) / roadmap / illumination.
(?) needs an enforcement point — five written statements did not bind
Do we have what we need? (entry gate)
MUST check the declared inputs of the rung about to start, and MUST push
back naming what is missing rather than proceeding on assumption.
MUST call 'Show where we are' rather than render a view of its own
Show where we are
MUST be invocable at any time, and MUST be produced at every phase-gate
close. MUST render have / need / progress for ONE rung AND for the whole
board. Never prose.
(?) the gate-close copy is the artifact of record for that gate — dated,
kept, diffable against the next one
Size work to a model
(?) every function that dispatches work MUST declare the model tier and
the effort it needs, and why. sized AFTER the work is specified, never
before. MUST NOT default to the top tier for difficulty alone
Where the work is written down
every function's output MUST have exactly one home, and its name MUST be
derivable without looking it up — know the subject, know the filename.
MUST date records of EVENTS, and MUST NOT date living documents.
the test: would rewriting this tomorrow be CORRECT, or would it be
FALSIFYING the record? correct -> living, no date, git history is the
archive. falsifying -> a record, dated, never rewritten again.
MUST state the git/vault split — git: machine-read, diffable, travels
with code. vault: human-read, assumes no prior context. never both.
MUST carry route and stage in front matter, so that route-specific
acceptance is machine-checkable rather than a human reading for it.
(?) MUST be reachable — an artifact nothing routes to is lost, not
stored. naming solves findability, NOT reachability. still open: the
6 Jul design doc that held 1 Aug's answer was perfectly well named.
What we ruled out, and why
MUST be its OWN artifact, reviewable in one pass — inside each solution doc,
'what have we already ruled out?' cannot be answered without reading all
of them.
MUST record the CONCEPT, not the code: what was tried or considered, why
it was eliminated, the evidence (a test OR an analysis — the same thing,
differing in cost), and the condition that would bring it back.
MUST be read in GROUNDING by every function that proposes anything. that
is what stops a dead option being re-proposed, and it is why this is not
a graveyard but an input.
MUST be captured as a BYPRODUCT of work already happening — a failed
verify IS the record. an artifact needing discipline to maintain goes
stale, and a stale 'already tried' list is worse than none.
MUST NOT record slips. the filter is: was it ever a candidate?
Stay in control of external tools
MUST name what is NOT being adopted before the tool is invoked
